Now it's clear why it looks confusing — **this is valid modern CSS, but GTK4 implements a frozen subset of the CSS spec, not all of it**.

Three specific gaps between "web CSS 2024" and "GTK4 CSS":

| What's in the file | Standard? | GTK 4.14 supports? |
|---|---|---|
| `:root { --blue-1: ... }` | CSS Custom Properties Level 1 | No — GTK has no document root concept; `:root` is rejected |
| `RGB(0 0 0 / 80%)` | CSS Color Level 4 (2018) | No — GTK 4.14 only accepts `rgba(0,0,0,0.8)` |
| `oklab(from @accent_bg_color ...)` | CSS Color Level 5 (2023) | No — needs GTK 4.16 |

GTK4's CSS engine was never meant to be a full browser renderer — it implements a **custom GTK-specific CSS dialect** that's evolved to track parts of the web spec over time. The adw-gtk3 theme started using `:root` and modern color syntax when those features landed in GTK 4.16 (released ~late 2024), but Ubuntu 24.04's GTK 4.14.5 doesn't have those additions yet.

So the errors aren't a bug in the theme or a mistake — they're a deliberate feature choice by adw-gtk3 v6.5 that requires the newer GTK. The only real fix is either:
- Get GTK 4.16 (not easy on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS)
- Use adw-gtk3 v5.x which was written against GTK 4.14 and doesn't use any of these newer features
